chapter1, 2 and 3.title: Chapter 1, 2 and 3:Introduction to Operating System and Linux and the User interface

questions.question: What is an Operating System (OS)?

options.b: A set of programs that manages computer hardware and software

questions.explanation: An Operating System is a set of programs that controls the execution of application programs and acts as an intermediary between users and computer hardware.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of an operating system?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Word is an application software, not an operating system.

questions.question: One objective of an operating system is to make the computer system convenient and easy to use.
questions.explanation: One major objective of an OS is to make the computer system convenient and easy for users.

questions.question: List the four components of a computer system.
questions.answerText: Hardware, Operating System, Application Programs, Users.
questions.explanation: These four components work together to make a computer system functional.

questions.question: Which component provides the means for proper use of computer hardware?
questions.explanation: The operating system manages and coordinates hardware resources.

questions.question: The bootstrap program is usually stored in ______.
questions.explanation: Bootstrap programs are stored in ROM or EEPROM firmware.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a bootstrap program?
questions.answerText: To initialize the system and load the operating system kernel into memory.
questions.explanation: The bootstrap program starts the computer and loads the OS.

questions.question: Which of the following is a function of an Operating System?
questions.explanation: All listed options are functions performed by an operating system.

questions.question: The OS prevents users from interfering with one another.
questions.explanation: An OS provides security and resource management among users.

questions.question: What type of operating system processes jobs in groups?
questions.explanation: Batch systems process jobs together as a batch.

questions.question: Give one example of a Real-Time Operating System application.
questions.explanation: The course material specifically mentioned the airline reservation system.

questions.question: Linux is an interactive, multi-user, multitasking operating system.
questions.explanation: Linux supports interaction, multiple users and multitasking.

questions.question: What does Multi-user mean in Linux?
questions.answerText: Linux allows many users to access the computer and differentiates between users.
questions.explanation: The system can identify and manage multiple users.

questions.question: What part of Linux manages processor, memory and disks?
questions.explanation: The kernel is responsible for managing system resources.

questions.question: The kernel remains in memory all the time.
questions.explanation: The Linux kernel stays loaded in memory while the system runs.

questions.question: Mention any four Linux distributions.
questions.explanation: These are examples listed in the COM115 note.

questions.question: Who developed UNIX?
questions.explanation: UNIX was developed by a team at Bell Labs.

questions.question: In what year did Bell Labs begin work on UNIX?
questions.explanation: Bell Labs began developing UNIX in 1969.

questions.question: Who created Linux?
questions.explanation: Linux was created by Linus Torvalds.

questions.question: Where was Linus Torvalds studying when he started Linux?
questions.explanation: Linus was a Computer Science student at the University of Helsinki.

questions.question: Linux was designed to comply with which standard?
questions.explanation: Linux was designed to comply with POSIX standards.

questions.question: Linux is a full UNIX clone.
questions.explanation: The note describes Linux as a full UNIX clone.

questions.question: Mention three movies whose production used Linux clusters.
questions.explanation: The note mentions Titanic and Shrek as examples.

questions.question: What does Open Source software allow users to do?
questions.explanation: Open Source software allows reading, modifying and sharing code.

questions.question: What is the license commonly used by Linux?
questions.explanation: Linux commonly uses the GNU Public License (GPL).

questions.question: State any four advantages of Linux.
questions.explanation: These are among the major Linux advantages discussed in the note.

questions.question: Linux is portable to any hardware platform.
questions.explanation: Linux can be adapted to many hardware platforms.

questions.question: What is one major disadvantage of Linux?
questions.answerText: Too many distributions and can be confusing for beginners.
questions.explanation: These are major Linux cons listed in the material.

questions.question: What does GNU stand for?
questions.explanation: GNU means GNU's Not UNIX.

questions.question: Which GNU tool is the GNU C Compiler?
questions.explanation: GCC stands for GNU C Compiler.

questions.question: What is Bash?
questions.explanation: Bash is the command interpreter used by Linux.

questions.question: Which package manager is associated with RedHat?
questions.explanation: RPM stands for RedHat Package Manager.

questions.question: Which Linux distribution runs directly from a CD-ROM?
questions.explanation: Knoppix can run without installation.

questions.question: Linux is written in which programming language?
questions.explanation: Linux is written primarily in C.

questions.question: What are the two basic modes of Linux?
questions.explanation: Linux can operate in either graphical or text mode.

questions.question: Why is logging in as root discouraged?
questions.explanation: Using root unnecessarily increases security risks.

questions.question: Which command changes a user's password?
questions.explanation: The passwd command changes a user's password.

questions.question: What does the pwd command do?
questions.explanation: pwd shows the current location in the file system.

questions.question: Which command displays the contents of a directory?
questions.explanation: ls lists files and folders in a directory.

questions.question: Which command displays manual pages?
questions.explanation: The man command displays online manual pages.

questions.question: Differentiate between man and info commands.
questions.answerText: man displays manual pages while info provides detailed GNU documentation.
questions.explanation: Info pages are often more detailed and easier to navigate.

chapter4.title: Chapter 4:Files and File system
chapter4.description: This chater contains so many questions because it covers a wide/long range of topics including in the Text book .

questions.question: What command displays information about disk partitions and mount points?
questions.explanation: The df command displays information about partitions, disk usage and mount points.

questions.question: A swap partition is used as an extension of physical memory.
questions.explanation: Swap partition provides virtual memory by using hard disk space.

questions.question: List the two major partition types in Linux.
questions.explanation: Linux mainly uses data partitions and swap partitions.

questions.question: What is the Linux partition number for swap partitions?
questions.explanation: Partition type 82 is used for swap space.

questions.question: What is the Linux partition number for data partitions?
questions.explanation: Partition type 83 is used for Linux data partitions.

questions.question: What is the root partition represented by in Linux?
questions.explanation: The root partition is represented by a single slash (/).

questions.question: Why are partitions important in Linux?
questions.answerText: For security, robustness, and preventing one partition from affecting the entire system.
questions.explanation: Partitioning protects the system from failures and improves organization.

questions.question: Which command is commonly used during installation to create Linux partitions?
questions.explanation: fdisk is commonly used for partition creation and management.

questions.question: A mount point is the location where a partition is attached to the file system.
questions.explanation: Mount points define where storage devices appear in the file system.

questions.question: What file stores partition mounting information during startup?
questions.explanation: The /etc/fstab file contains mount configuration information.

questions.question: What command is used to attach a partition to the Linux file system?
questions.explanation: The mount command connects partitions or storage devices to the file system.

questions.question: The Linux file system is usually represented as a ______ structure.
questions.explanation: Linux file systems are commonly visualized as a tree structure.

questions.question: What is the topmost directory in Linux called?
questions.explanation: The root directory (/) is the top of the Linux file system hierarchy.

questions.question: Mention any four subdirectories found under the root directory.
questions.explanation: These are common root-level directories.

questions.question: What command shows the partition containing the current directory?
questions.explanation: df . shows disk information about the current directory's partition.

questions.question: What is an inode?
questions.answerText: A data structure that stores information about a file except its name and directory.
questions.explanation: Inodes store ownership, permissions, location and timestamps.

questions.question: Which information is NOT stored in an inode?
questions.explanation: File names are stored separately in directory structures.

questions.question: Every partition has its own set of inodes.
questions.explanation: Inode numbers are unique only within a partition.

questions.question: State four pieces of information stored in an inode.
questions.explanation: These are key attributes maintained in an inode.

questions.question: Which environment variable contains executable search paths?
questions.explanation: PATH contains directories searched for executable commands.

questions.question: What command displays the contents of PATH?
questions.explanation: echo $PATH shows the search path configuration.

questions.question: Differentiate between absolute and relative paths.
questions.answerText: Absolute paths start from '/', while relative paths start from the current directory.
questions.explanation: Absolute paths uniquely identify locations; relative paths depend on current position.

questions.question: Which symbol represents the current directory?
questions.explanation: A single dot (.) represents the current directory.

questions.question: Which symbol represents the parent directory?
questions.explanation: Double dots (..) represent the parent directory.

questions.question: What does the command ./configure mean?
questions.answerText: Run the configure program located in the current directory.
questions.explanation: The dot slash specifies execution from the current location.

questions.question: What is a shell?
questions.explanation: A shell allows users to communicate with the operating system.

questions.question: Which shell is the default GNU shell on Linux?
questions.explanation: Bash stands for Bourne Again Shell and is Linux's standard shell.

questions.question: List any four Linux shell types.
questions.explanation: These are common shell types available on Linux.

questions.question: Which command shows the current shell being used?
questions.explanation: The SHELL environment variable stores the current shell.

questions.question: What environment variable stores the user's home directory?
questions.explanation: HOME contains the path to the user's home directory.

questions.question: What symbol is used as shorthand for the home directory?
questions.explanation: The tilde (~) represents the current user's home directory.

questions.question: What command displays disk quota information?
questions.explanation: quota -v shows quota limits assigned to a user.

questions.question: Most Linux configuration files are stored in which directory?
questions.explanation: The /etc directory contains configuration files.

questions.question: Which command displays the contents of configuration files?
questions.explanation: cat displays the contents of text files.

questions.question: Which directory contains device files in Linux?
questions.explanation: All devices are represented in the /dev directory.

questions.question: What directory contains log files in Linux?
questions.explanation: System and application logs are stored in /var/log.

questions.question: Why is /var usually placed on a separate partition?
questions.answerText: To protect critical system files and manage frequently changing data safely.
questions.explanation: It prevents variable files from filling the entire system partition.

questions.question: Files stored in /tmp may be deleted automatically.
questions.explanation: /tmp files can be removed during reboot or cleanup operations.

questions.question: What is the safer location for temporary files according to the note?
questions.explanation: /var/tmp is generally safer for temporary file storage.

questions.question: What directory commonly contains website files on Linux servers?
questions.explanation: Web pages, scripts and images are usually stored in /var/www.

questions.question: What is the default file manager in GNOME?
questions.explanation: Nautilus is GNOME's default file manager.

questions.question: Which command removes a single file in Linux?
questions.explanation: The rm command is used to remove files.

questions.question: Which command removes an empty directory?
questions.explanation: The rmdir command removes empty directories.

questions.question: Why is the rm command considered dangerous?
questions.answerText: Because deleted files are usually permanently removed and cannot easily be recovered.
questions.explanation: Linux shell does not normally provide a recycle bin.

questions.question: Which option makes rm ask for confirmation before deleting files?
questions.explanation: The -i option enables interactive confirmation.

questions.question: The asterisk (*) wildcard represents ______.
questions.explanation: The * wildcard matches any number of characters.

questions.question: The question mark (?) wildcard represents ______.
questions.explanation: The ? wildcard matches exactly one character.

questions.question: What feature allows Bash to complete filenames automatically?
questions.explanation: Bash can automatically complete filenames when the Tab key is pressed.

questions.question: Which command helps locate executable programs in the PATH?
questions.explanation: The which command identifies the location of executable programs.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the find command?
questions.answerText: To search for files and directories based on specified criteria.
questions.explanation: find can search by name, size, date, and other attributes.

questions.question: Which command searches files using an indexed database and is faster than find?
questions.explanation: locate searches a prebuilt database and returns results quickly.

questions.question: What is one disadvantage of the locate command?
questions.answerText: Its database is updated periodically, so newly created files may not appear immediately.
questions.explanation: locate relies on an indexed database rather than real-time searching.

questions.question: Which command is used for filtering text and searching patterns?
questions.explanation: grep searches text for matching patterns.

questions.question: What does grep stand for?
questions.explanation: grep is a powerful text searching utility.

questions.question: Which character is used as an escape character in Bash?
questions.explanation: The backslash removes the special meaning of characters.

questions.question: Which command is known as the GNU version of more?
questions.explanation: less provides enhanced viewing features compared to more.

questions.question: State one advantage of less over more.
questions.answerText: It allows backward scrolling and search highlighting.
questions.explanation: less has more advanced navigation features.

questions.question: Which command displays the first lines of a file?
questions.explanation: head displays the beginning of a file.

questions.question: Which command continuously monitors changes to a file?
questions.explanation: tail -f is commonly used to monitor log files.

questions.question: Differentiate between a hard link and a symbolic link.
questions.answerText: A hard link points directly to the inode while a symbolic link points to the file path.
questions.explanation: Hard links share the same inode, while symbolic links are separate pointer files.

questions.question: Which command creates a symbolic link?
questions.explanation: The ln -s command creates symbolic (soft) links.

questions.question: A user wants to find all files named 'project.txt' in the /home directory and its subdirectories. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: The find command searches directories and subdirectories using specified criteria.

questions.question: A student wants to quickly search for a file that was created several days ago. Which command will usually return results faster?
questions.explanation: locate uses a database and is generally faster than find.

questions.question: A user receives a 'Permission Denied' error while trying to run a script. Which command is most likely needed?
questions.explanation: The script may not have execute permission and chmod can grant it.

questions.question: A system administrator wants to monitor new entries being added continuously to a log file. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: tail -f continuously displays updates to a file.

questions.question: A user wants to display only the first 20 lines of a large text file. Which command is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: head displays the beginning portion of a file.

questions.question: A lecturer asks you to create a shortcut to a file located on another partition. What type of link should you create?
questions.explanation: Symbolic links can span across different partitions.

questions.question: A user deletes the original file that a symbolic link points to. What happens to the symbolic link?

options.d: The link becomes a hard link

questions.explanation: A symbolic link depends on the target file path.

questions.question: A file has permissions rwxr-xr-x. Who can modify the file?
questions.explanation: The owner has write permission while group and others only have read and execute permissions.

questions.question: A student wants to search for the word 'Linux' inside a text document. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: grep searches for patterns inside files.

questions.question: A user wants to know the location of the executable program 'python'. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: which shows the location of executable programs.
